stimulus.body: A 2011 report on 600 teenagers in the Netherlands found the top share earned 79% of income, while the bottom share earned 27%.

questions.stem: Which conclusion about income gap in Netherlands does the 2011 data support?

options.text: The 2011 Netherlands data support income inequality as the explanation for the income gap pattern.
The 2011 Netherlands data support Gini index as the explanation for the income gap pattern.
options.misconception: treats the index as a percentage of national income

options.text: The 2011 Netherlands data support wealth as the explanation for the income gap pattern.
options.misconception: uses wealth and income as interchangeable terms

options.text: The 2011 Netherlands data support progressive tax as the explanation for the income gap pattern.
options.misconception: assumes any tax reduces inequality automatically

questions.explanation: The unequal distribution of earnings across a population. questions.hint: Ask what would have to be true for both figures to hold.
